title: Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers at t at Most 7
summary: Optimal security is known for t at least 8, while tightness for key-alternating ciphers at t at most 7 remains open.

formal_statement.body: For key-alternating ciphers with $(t-2)$-wise independent sub-keys, the security bound is optimal for $t \ge 8$, whereas tightness for $t \le 7$ remains unresolved. The open task is to determine whether this optimal-security result extends to the remaining parameter values $t \le 7$.

scope.domain: Security bounds for key-alternating block ciphers with correlated sub-keys.
parameters: t: indexes the sub-key independence level and separates the known and unresolved regimes
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the optimal-security result extends to t ≤ 7.

citations.label: Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys

progress.summary: The source reports that the security bound becomes optimal for t ≥ 8 and explicitly leaves tightness for t ≤ 7 open.
citation_labels: Stefano Tessaro et al., Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys
